title: Sheaf-level first-residue pushout
statement:
theorem internal_first_residue_sheaf_pushout
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (e : Mon.mk (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E 1) ≅
      Mon.mk (IntegralModelsStacks.discreteObj
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1)))
    (he : (IntegralModelsStacks.scalarMap l E X ≫
        coefficientMap (IntegralConstantModel.pointComparison l E).inv.hom X) ≫
        (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X 0 ≫ coefficientMap e.hom.hom X) =
      IntegralModelsStacks.residueMap l E X) :
    let a := IntegralModelsStacks.scalarMap l E X ≫
      coefficientMap (IntegralConstantModel.pointComparison l E).inv.hom X
    IsPushout (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X a)
      (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X (IntegralModelsStacks.residueMap l E X))
      (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X
        (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X 0 ≫ coefficientMap e.hom.hom X)) (𝟙 _)

proof.text: The constant completion square is a pushout of commutative ring sheaves: on each object the quotient is surjective and the kernel of the completion projection is the ideal generated by the scalar images of the constant quotient kernel. For any compatible ring cocone, kill that ideal and use quotient surjectivity to prove the required factorization; its uniqueness follows from the identity lower leg. Sectionwise pushouts give the sheaf pushout by the proved SectionwisePushout theorem.

Use the proved discreteRingIso, completedScalar_projection, residueLiftIso and their normalization calculations from the integralModels_flat_residue module to identify the actual scalar and residue maps with the constant completion diagram. Transport the pushout through these isomorphisms.

The specified pointComparison gives an isomorphism on reconstructed small-site rings. The supplied commuting-square equality fixes the residue normalization. The pushout universal property shows its upper-right map is the canonical one, and transport along pointComparison proves the result.

proof_origin.place: ring-valued completion pushout and normalized residue square; Lean proof written in this delivery

    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (e : Mon.mk (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E 1) ≅

statement_change.what: The original IsPushout was in abelian sheaves, whereas quotient base change gives a pushout of commutative ring sheaves. Its additive kernel would consist only of locally constant uniformizer multiples, while the actual continuous quotient kernel contains all continuous uniformizer multiples. Also an arbitrary ring isomorphism e can be twisted by a nontrivial automorphism of a finite residue extension and then the square does not commute. Correct the category to the reconstructed commutative ring sheaves on the equivalent small site and require the specified residue isomorphism to make the actual square commute. The sole consumer constructs the canonical constant-function isomorphism and proves this equality; its public conclusion is unchanged.

citers.note: Adapted in this delivery to use the canonical firstResidueIso and its proved normalization; the existential ring pushout statement is unchanged. No separate additive-pushout transport is used.

old_proof.text: Identify the continuous integral ring with the normalized inverse-limit completion and identify its first quotient with the finite constant quotient using flatness and quotient comparisons.
Use naturality of the constant-function coefficient map to obtain the residue square and its tensor universal property.
